description: Non-fee regulatory inputs: merchant classification and the derived-state rules that gate nil-MDR eligibility. Classification is DERIVED from transaction history, not read from merchant configuration, because the P2PM to P2M transition depends on a rolling three-month test.

merchant_classification.name: NPCI P2PM small-merchant classification
merchant_classification.evaluation: A merchant is P2PM while monthly inward UPI credits stay at or below Rs 1,00,000. Exceeding that limit in three CONSECUTIVE months transitions the merchant to P2M. A single large payment does not by itself change classification.
assumptions: The three-consecutive-month transition rule is reported by BusinessToday but we have not read the NPCI circular directly.

The reverse transition (P2M back to P2PM) is not described by any source we found. We do NOT model it; a merchant that has become P2M stays P2M, and any case turning on a reverse transition escalates.

source.document: P2PM classification and transition under the UPI MDR framework effective 15 Oct 2026

regime_boundaries.description: MDR begins applying to RuPay Credit Card on UPI above Rs 2,000, MCC-driven.
Section 10A PSS Act converted from a blanket zero-MDR prohibition into an enabling provision; Government may notify which modes stay protected.
MoF/DFS notification protects UPI up to Rs 2,000 and RuPay debit at all amounts.
NPCI UPI P2M MDR of 0.4 percent above Rs 2,000 commences. NOT in force as at the demo date of 2026-09-16.
